reviews.title: Racist
reviews.text:
As a longtime customer, I find the recent Converse advertising deeply disturbing and unacceptable.

This is not about one image viewed in isolation. Multiple Converse advertisements have featured imagery that evokes some of the most horrific symbols of anti-Black racial violence: a white pointed shape resembling a KKK hood alongside dangling black shoes, shoes hanging from a tree, and imagery involving a black tennis ball being crushed while surrounded by white tennis balls.

Regardless of the intent behind these creative decisions, I cannot understand how imagery with these racial associations made it through the concept, photography, editing, review, and approval process of a global company.

Converse has apologized and acknowledged that it got this wrong, but removing an advertisement after public outrage does not address the larger concern: How did this happen, and what safeguards failed?

As Converse’s parent company, Nike should publicly address what changes are being made to ensure culturally and historically informed review of advertising before campaigns are released. Accountability should include examining who has a voice in the creative and approval process and whether those teams include people equipped to recognize imagery associated with America’s history of racial terror.

Customers should not have to point these things out after an advertisement goes live. Nike and Converse can and should do better.

reviews.title: Terrible Launch Experience for a New Customer
reviews.text:
I downloaded the Nike app specifically to purchase the new Nike Mind slides when they released on August 20 at 9:00 AM. I literally set an alarm for 8:55 AM, had the app open before the release, and clicked on them the moment they became available.

I selected my size immediately and entered my information as fast as possible. The slides were still showing as available while I was checking out, so I expected the order to go through. Instead of receiving a purchase confirmation, I got a message saying something along the lines of, “We’ll let you know if we can fulfill your order.”

At that point, I already knew what was coming.

A few moments later, Nike notified me that they could not fulfill the order because the product was sold out. That is extremely disappointing. If I clicked on the product immediately at release and made it all the way through checkout while my size was still being shown as available, there should be some type of temporary reservation system while the customer completes payment. A release should not come down to who can type an address or process payment a fraction of a second faster—especially when bots, resellers, and scalpers are competing for the exact same inventory.

What makes this even worse is that I was a new direct Nike customer. I normally do not purchase directly through Nike, but I genuinely liked this release and wanted to buy it directly from the company. Instead, my first experience was waking up specifically for the release, being ther

reviews.title: You ruined someone’s special moments
reviews.text:
May 3rd is my guy’s birthday, and today at exactly 10:00 AM, the moment you released the Nike Mind (black and blue fade), I hit the payment button. I was on time. I was ready. I did everything right.

For the past two weeks, I’ve been constantly checking the Nike App just to make sure I don’t miss this drop. I even saved my card details and shipping address in advance so there would be zero delay from my side.

But your app completely ruined the experience.

Every time I submitted the payment, it showed pending, then checking availability, and then suddenly said the item was unavailable. I tried multiple times, and the same thing kept happening — while the app still showed my size as available.

How does that even make sense? If I clicked exactly at 10:00 AM and submitted my payment on time, how is the stock already gone while you’re still letting me proceed to checkout?

You made me feel like I was going to get it — and then took it away at the last second.

This wasn’t just a purchase. That guy literally worked so hard to get me the best birthday gift, and it honestly hurts that I couldn’t get what he wanted because of this system. You didn’t just lose a sale — you ruined a special moment for both of us.

And it’s not even cheap — it’s around $249 in stores. For that price, at least give customers a fair and transparent experience. Please don’t play with the emotions of middle-class people who are genuinely trying to afford something special.

This is really, really sad and

reviews.title: Zero chat support response
reviews.text: So as a business owner I have literally spent tens of thousands of dollars on this app. I had issues with orders where checking my inventory I was missing a lot of orders and when checking the app the order show as “shipped” not delivered. When reaching out to chat support I would always end up having to re explain to a new representative because somehow there would always be an error or “no connection” while on WiFi. But no problem trying to place an order once kicked out of chat. But what’s more alarming is they completely started ignoring my chats.. till this day it’s been about 2 years almost and I have not gotten a single response to over 30 attempts and messages sent. I had a lot of double orders as well and when returning there’s a whole mix up of return started even though I sent the shoes already. Or it will say returned at store even though it literally has tracking details. This is very upsetting and frustrating at the same time but given the amount of support and hard earned money I’ve spent with Nike it’s very disheartening to be disrespected like this. Wouldn’t expect this from a top tier elite corporation like this.

reviews.title: Various problems actually paying
reviews.text:
What Apple thinks is a valid phone number and what the app thinks is a valid phone number are not the same (hint: Apple is right), so Apple Pay, the default option, doesn’t work.

Entering card details automatically on iOS is not possible, so had to enter card details manually, which is error-prone and less secure.

Won’t deliver to PO box but it does not tell you that, only that the address is invalid (not true), so had to enter alternate address (ironically this is less physically secure, hence the PO Box).

The address form is badly coded so you can’t automatically complete the address from iOS. But the address lookup is also bad so my address was not visible, only four other invalid addresses (never had this problem elsewhere).

Manually editing the address is pure guesswork because you can’t see what you’re doing due to interactions of the keyboard and the address lookup UI.

All in all very painful add really poor quality QA on the most important section of the app.

reviews.title: The dumbest most solvable issue
reviews.text: I don’t know if this is a review on the app itself or an issue with the lack of common sense on the part of the designers. Either way. It is near impossible to buy a matching set. Bare w me. I bought a pair of sweatpants. All I want is a matching hoodie. Simple right? No. You can’t filter by color bc of course there are a million variations of grey and blue. Even if you select the sweats you already purchased there isn’t an icon on the bottom pointing you to the recommended matching top. Both the designers of the app as well as of the clothes themselves missed a big opportunity here. I’d love to buy a few different matching top options, cropped hoodie, zip up, ribbed top.. come on guys. Now I’m stuck with mismatched grey sweatpants and sweater looking cheap even though it’s not. It’s so annoying and such an easy fix on their end. I would expect more from a brand that’s been around eons.
